title: Numerical boundary-order recovery by cancellation of two test weights
statement: Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and let $E$ be a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary [def-trf-strict-normal-crossings-boundary] transverse to $N$ (its local equations restrict to distinct coordinate parameters on $N$). Let $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ be coherent and $d\ge1$. Write $\operatorname{ord}_x I=\sup\{q\ge0:I_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with value $\infty$ for zero, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(I,d)=\{x:\operatorname{ord}_xI\ge d\}$. A test transformation is an open restriction, a smooth-center blowup in cosupport with normal crossings with $E$, a product with a line adjoining its zero section to $E$, or a blowup of the intersection of two boundary hypersurfaces. For a cosupport blowup use the strict transform of $N$ and the ideal $e^{-d}\sigma^*I$, where $e$ is the exceptional equation; for the last two operations use ordinary pullback. Two such data on the same ambient scheme and with the same ordered boundary are test equivalent if their finite test sequences coincide. Let $(N,I,d)$ and $(P,J,b)$ be test equivalent, where $P$ is also smooth and has the same local dimension as $N$.  After any common finite sequence [def-trf-common-marked-test-sequence], write $(T,M_T,P_T)$ for its endpoints, $d_T,b_T$ for their marks, and take arbitrary support points $x\in M_T$, $y\in P_T$ with the same ambient image in both cosupports. For every current boundary label $H$, $\operatorname{ord}_{H,x}I_T\,b_T=\operatorname{ord}_{H,y}J_T\,d_T$ in $\mathbb N_\infty$.

proof.text: Apply the two-test witness theorem. If both boundary orders are infinite, multiplication by the positive marks leaves both products infinite. If both are zero both products vanish.
